name: Spring Hora Queen
body:
SPRING HORA QUEEN
CR 13

This beautiful woman dances among the flowers without leaving a trace; her hair, skin, and eyes match the green, gold, pink, and blue of a flowery meadow, as do the veils she wears.

XP 25,600
CG Medium fey
Init +9; Senses low-light vision; Perception +28
Aura charming beauty (30 ft., DC 27)

DEFENSE

AC 28, touch 16, flat-footed 22 (+5 Dex, +1 dodge, +12 natural)
hp 187(22d6+110); fast healing 10
Fort +14, Ref +18, Will +16
DR 10/cold iron; Immune aging effects
Weaknesses spring bound

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee 2 blooming quarterstaves +17 (3d6+5 bludgeoning +3d6 positive energy)
Ranged 2 rays of life +17 (6d8 positive energy)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 20th; concentration +16)

Constant—speak with animals, speak with plants
At will—know direction, light, pass without trace
1/day—alarm, animal messenger, bestow curse (DC 20), commune with nature, entangle (DC 17), euphoric tranquility (DC 24), true seeing

Druid Spells Prepared (CL 13th; concentration +16)

7th-level—heal
6th-level—blazing rainbow, liveoak
5th-level—baleful polymorph (DC 18), tree stride, wall of thorns
4th-level—arboreal hammer, cure serious wounds, freedom of movement, vermin shape II
3rd-level—cure moderate wounds, daylight, neutralize poison, remove disease, vermin shape I
2nd-level—euphoric cloud (DC 16), forest friend, soothing word, summon nature’s ally II, tree shape
1st-level—charm animal (DC 14), cure light wounds, longstrider, summon nature’s ally I, tripvine (DC 14)
0th-level—detect magic, guidance, stabilize, virtue

STATISTICS

Str 14, Dex 21, Con 20, Int 17, Wis 17, Cha 22
Base Atk +11; CMB +16, CMD 29
Feats Agile Maneuvers, Combat Casting, Dodge, Great Fortitude, Improved Initiative, Mobility, Sidestep, Spell Focus (conjuration), Weapon Finesse, Weapon Focus (autumn sickle, ray of decay)
Skills Acrobatics +30, Climb +27, Diplomacy +31, Escape Artist +30, Knowledge (nature) +28, Perception +28, Sense Motive +28, Stealth +30, Survival +25
Languages Common, Elven, Sylvan; speak with animals, speak with plants
SQ spring’s safekeeping

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Charming Beauty (Su)

This ability affects all humanoids within 30 feet of the spring hora queen. Those who look directly at the queen must succeed on a DC 27 Fortitude save or be under the effect of charm monster for 1 minute and then fascinated for a maximum of 1 hour. The queen can suppress or resume this ability as a free action. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Spellcasting

The spring hora queen casts spells as a 13th-level druid, but can’t swap out prepared spells to cast summon spells.

Spring Bound (Su)

During autumnal months, the spring hora queen gains the sickened condition.

Spring’s Safekeeping (Su)

As an immediate action after a spring hora queen or an ally within 30 feet of the queen that it can see fails a saving throw, attack roll, or skill check, the queen grants an enhancement bonus to the saving throw based on the time of year. The bonus is +4 during the month of the vernal equinox, +2 during the month before or after the vernal equinox, and +1 during any time other than the autumnal equinox month, during which this ability doesn’t function. The spring hora queen can’t use this ability again for 1d4 rounds.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate forests
Organization solitary or ring (1 + 1-24 spring horai)
Treasure double (2 blooming quarterstaves, feather token [tree], other treasure)

The Horai in the Greek myth were nymphs who danced around the Sun’s chariot, representing the seasons of the year and the hours of the day (the word “hour” derives from the Ancient Greek and Latin Hora). There were most commonly three of them: Thallo, Auxo, and Carpo (“Bloom” for Spring, “Increaser” for Summer, and “Reaper of Fruits” for Autumn). In other versions, they were the embodiment of the good effects of law and order (symbolized by Apollo) on the world of mortals, and their names were Eunomia (“Good Governance”), Dike (“Justice”), and Eirene (“Peace”). In Pathfinder’s rules, the stats for the Summer Hora and the Summer Hora Queen were given in the Faerie Bestiary: here we present horai for the remaining three seasons, and their respective Queens. Maybe the nymphs of Order could be discussed in a future issue of this magazine?
